guards.central_guards: app_factory.py:1093-1149 (guard factory, super_admin-only bypass), 1211-1267 and 1312-1332 (all guarded blueprints incl. finance/manager/booking/procurement/portal/integration)
guards.notes: Blueprint-local guard_module in services/feature_gate_service.py:198-217 bypasses tenant admin for billing/reporting/appointments/inventory, but the central guard in app_factory.py:1115-1137 re-checks the same module and denies tenant admins; both run for all eight locally-guarded blueprints.

test_summary.skip_reason: tests/test_notification_rls_lifecycle.py:55 - current database user is superuser; RLS is bypassed (4 skips). RLS behaviour for that subset is covered by the other RLS tests and by the pg_catalog policy check.

risks.title: product_profile_code stores canonical category, not the purchased package slug
risks.detail: 16 of 23 package tenants have product_profile_code set to a canonical ProductProfile category (e.g. pkg-hospital -> multi_department_center, pkg-billing-only -> custom) rather than the slug of the package they bought. The purchase boundary itself is correct because app/core/module/validators.py:86-108 reads the active SubscriptionLine first, and all 23 tenants have one, but every legacy/fallback path that resolves get_bundle_for_profile(product_profile_code) sees the wrong bundle.
risks.impact: Owner console labels the wrong bundle; legacy entitlement fallback and admin/manager dashboard routing can under-grant or misroute for those tenants if the subscription/projection is absent.

risks.title: Legacy bundle row private_doctor_clinic has NULL max_users/max_patients
risks.detail: product_bundles row slug=private_doctor_clinic has max_users=NULL and max_patients=NULL while _PRODUCT_PROFILE_SEED (app/core/tenant/models.py:445-452) defines 3 and 500. package_version_limits version 1 supplies the correct 3/500 (storage_gb=5 and api_calls_per_month=10000 are defined only in package_version_limits, not in the seed). All 23 package tenants have active subscription lines, so EntitlementResolver.get_effective_limits() returns the correct package-version limits; only the legacy fallback (app/core/saas/legacy_adapter.py:72-77) would see unlimited.
risks.impact: A tenant whose subscription line is missing, ended, or not yet migrated would have no effective user/patient cap on the legacy path.

risks.title: Service-level module decorators bypass tenant admin for non-clinical modules
risks.detail: require_module(), require_module_route() and guard_module() skip the check for role admin/super_admin/owner/platform_owner when the module is billing, reporting, appointments or inventory. The central blueprint guard only exempts super_admin and re-checks the same modules, so tenant admins are denied on all guarded blueprints; the bypass is latent and would become live on any new blueprint guarded only by the local decorator.
risks.impact: Future route using only require_module/guard_module can be opened to a tenant admin without the module in the bundle.

risks.title: Compliance APIs are role-gated but not module-gated
risks.detail: compliance_bp is registered without _add_guard_once and reads Patient, Visit, Appointment, LabResult, RadiologyResult, Prescription, MedicalRecord, PatientAllergy and PatientConsent. Access is restricted by @role_required(super_admin/admin/manager) only. ORM tenant_filter module scope still empties tables no active module touches (app/shared/tenant_filter.py:256-286, 624-630), so no data was observed to leak, but the module boundary is not enforced at the route layer.
risks.impact: A raw-SQL or bypassed read added to this blueprint would expose out-of-package clinical tables.

risks.title: Unguarded blueprints read tables absent from MODULE_REGISTRY
risks.detail: order_set_bp and device_bp have no module guard, and the tables they use (order_sets, order_set_items, best_practice_advisories, iot_devices, iot_readings, medical_devices) are not listed by any ModuleMeta, so tenant_filter._table_out_of_scope() cannot restrict them by purchased modules. Only login_required/role_required and tenant_id filtering apply.
risks.impact: Any authenticated user with the required role can read/write these resources regardless of the tenant package (e.g. a billing-only tenant can register devices and order sets).

risks.title: Recent booking-to-visit conversion writes clinical tables from an appointments-only route
risks.detail: Commit cdb6ecb8 added convert_booking_to_visit on booking_bp (guarded by appointments). It creates Patient/Visit and a MedicalRecord and transitions the visit to IN_PROGRESS. For pkg-billing-only (appointments + billing, no doctor/reception) tenant_filter._assert_table_writable() refuses the visits/medical_records write (app/shared/tenant_filter.py:460-479, 794-818), so no data leak occurs; the endpoint only flashes an error.
risks.impact: Functional break for appointments-only bundles; if the write bypass is ever used, it would create clinical care data outside the purchased package.
